hook: A U.S. military MISREP filed from the Djibouti operational area documents two 'round white hot' UAPs traveling south at approximately 240 nautical miles per hour, observed at 1653Z at a precise MGRS grid coordinate. Six of the report's seven pages are fully redacted under FOIA exemption 1.4(a).
why_it_matters: This report represents a recent (2025) military UAP sighting formally channeled to AARO via the standardized MISREP process, demonstrating that the reporting pipeline established under the UAP disclosure framework is actively being used in operational theater settings. The SECRET//REL TO USA, FIN, SWE, FVEY, NATO classification caveat indicates the incident was shared across the Five Eyes intelligence community as well as Finland and Sweden — both recent NATO additions — suggesting UAP data is being integrated into allied intelligence sharing arrangements. The near-total redaction of six pages limits independent assessment of sensor data, reporting chain, and follow-on actions.

key_findings.finding: Two UAPs described as round and 'white hot' were observed moving south at approximately 240 nautical miles per hour (roughly 276 mph) at a specific MGRS grid location.

quotes.text: OBS 2X ROUND WHITE HOT UAPS DYNAMIC SOUTH AT APPROX 240NM/HOUR IVO 35SQT3423692957.

key_findings.finding: The GENTEXT section repeats the UAP observation in a second bullet with slightly less descriptive detail, suggesting the MISREP format separates the physical description from the event narrative.

quotes.text: OBS 2X UAPS DYNAMIC SOUTH AT APPROX 240NM/HOUR IVO 35SQT3423692957.

key_findings.finding: The report is classified SECRET and explicitly shared with Finland, Sweden, Five Eyes, and NATO — a broad allied distribution unusual for a single-incident operational sighting.

OBS 2X ROUND WHITE HOT UAPS DYNAMIC SOUTH AT APPROX 240NM/HOUR IVO 35SQT3423692957.

key_findings.finding: Six of the report's seven pages are entirely withheld under FOIA exemption 1.4(a), which covers properly classified national security information, leaving sensor type, platform identity, follow-on actions, and reporting chain unknown.

The observation time is recorded to the minute in Zulu time, and the location is given as a 10-digit MGRS coordinate (35SQT3423692957), indicating high-precision geolocation consistent with military sensor or operator positioning capability.
